caveats: Measure is shipment weight in kg (gross weight on most US bills of lading, not contained Sb); 402 of 431 used rows carry a weight field.

13 rows are value-imputed: 12 Korea Zinc Korean-export rows (kg = value / USD 397,480 x 19,677 kg) and one Amalgamet Japan-source row (USD 6.06M / 2024 median USD 19.89/kg = ~305 t, a large single-month spike in eu-traders 2024-02).
Coverage is partial: Sayari holds US import bills of lading (mostly ocean freight) plus some partner-country export records. It is not a full US import total; Comtrade/USGS levels are higher.
Many nodes are lumpy: months with shipments per node (of 46) are in raw.monthsWithShipments; zeros are 'no recorded shipment', not measured zero imports.

in-chemico falls to ~0 in 2026: Sayari's India export source thins after 2025-12, and a Chemico lot shipped via Spain (arrived 2026-10-27, seen in a separate Sayari query) is not in the pulled HS-811010 set. Treat 2026 Chemico zeros as a likely data lag, not a confirmed stop.
Korea Zinc only appears from 2025-07, so its series is mostly zeros; covariance with other nodes will be driven by the regime change.
Node assignment uses departure country (or shipper address); traders/forwarders hide true origin, so China-linked volume is likely understated in eu-traders, sea-transit and other.
Dedup across sources is heuristic (month +-1, kg within 15%); some double counts or wrongly dropped lots may remain.
Sayari date_from filter was loose (rows from 2020-2022 returned); those were dropped locally.
Oxides (HS 282580, 1,471 shipments, the main post-ban transshipment product per Reuters) and ore (261710) are NOT in the volume series.

Tier-2 'reported' shares are shipment-count shares of a country's antimony-ore imports (Sayari facets), used as proxies for the tier-1 node; not tonnage and not company-specific (receiver filters were not honoured).
Thai Unipet's Chinese ownership comes from Reuters reporting via Tavily, not from Sayari ownership records.
